hints: When is the type of `x` known: while compiling or while running?
exercises.solution: Each distinct argument type produces a separate instantiation of `show`, compiled and type-checked on its own. If the body does something an `i32` cannot do, only that instantiation fails to compile. This is the same model as C++ templates, written in ordinary Zig.

exercises.prompt: A function contains `if (builtin.mode == .debug) expensiveCheck(data);`. What happens in a build with `-O fast`?

options.label: The condition is known at compile time to be false, so the call is removed and costs nothing at run time.
options.feedback: Yes. `builtin.mode` is a comptime constant, so the branch is resolved during compilation.

options.label: The condition is tested every time the function runs, but the call is skipped.
options.feedback: Not yet — there is nothing to test at run time; the compiler already knows the answer.

options.label: It does not compile, because `if` cannot test the build mode.
options.feedback: Not yet — this is the idiomatic replacement for C's `#ifdef DEBUG`.

options.label: `expensiveCheck` still runs, because Zig never removes code.
options.feedback: Not yet — branches on comptime-known conditions are pruned, and the untaken branch is not even analysed.

exercises.solution: `@import("builtin").mode` is a comptime constant describing the current build. An `if` on it is resolved by the compiler: in a fast build the branch is false, so `expensiveCheck(data)` is not compiled into the program at all. This is how Zig code does conditional compilation without a preprocessor.
